note_tweet.text:
[RUMOR] An OpenAI staffer says ChatGPT dots is starting to test 1Password, so your agent can log in for you. 🔐

On Nov 16, James Sun, who works on dots at OpenAI, posted, "We're starting to test 1password in dots!" He said the goal is to make it easy for a dot to do tasks that require a login, while keeping credentials secure, and that OpenAI is excited to roll this out more broadly soon. In follow up replies, he said it currently works with individual accounts, and that the team is working with 1Password on shared and business accounts.

1Password itself replied on Nov 18 that it is "still rolling 1Password out in Dots," and that "we don't have a way to get started just yet." That is an official confirmation that a rollout is underway, and also a warning that you cannot sign up today.

This is a test, not a launch. No public start date, plan, or region has been announced, and business vaults are not included yet.

Source: https://t.co/GD5g0GiOVI

Image: @nxtday

Would you let an AI agent fill a site login from your password manager? 🔑

Sure — you can pass this along to my CTO. He’s currently rolling out Copilot, Claude, and ChatGPT Dots. As part of that effort, he has a proof of concept showing that an app upgrade project which would normally take teams a year was completed in three months. The business is validating it now. 

In the workflow, a user story is submitted and one of the three AI agents writes the code. Code commits are then added to the discussion tab of the user story for traceability. (This traceability step leverages one of the practices my team put in place with an automated script — something we need because we don’t have an all-in-one solution.)

His next focus is adoption within QA. Once that’s underway, my teams will be next for change management, release management, DevOps, and IT governance.

Given that we’re heavily regulated, I’m starting with a small use case and building my backlog from there.
